body:
Found 2026-08-09 in adversarial review of the Kobo annotation read design
(`notes/KOBO-NICKEL-ANNOTATION-READ-DESIGN-2026-08-09.md`). Applies to ANY future server-authored
response on `GET /api/v3/content/<id>/annotations`. Not a defect in shipped code today — we do not
author that response yet — but it must be designed for before we ever do.

Mechanism. [OBSERVED] The device issues the annotations GET on book open, before any highlight is
uploaded and before `checkforchanges` (live capture 2026-08-09 14:51:31). [OBSERVED] CWNG persists
an annotation only when its PATCH arrives (`cps/readingservices.py:347-385`). [INFERRED] So with two
Kobos on one account: device A holds a locally-created annotation it has NOT yet PATCHed; device B
has meanwhile changed CWNG's snapshot. A performs its pre-upload GET, and receives a snapshot that
is internally complete server-side but INCOMPLETE relative to A. If Nickel treats absence from an
authoritative set as deletion, A erases its own new annotation before it was ever uploaded.

Why the obvious mitigation does not work: transactionally snapshotting the server (the
"concurrent PATCH while GET is built" case) does not help, because the missing write is outside the
server transaction entirely. This is a distributed lost-update race, not an inconsistent-read race.

Why we cannot currently detect it: the `checkforchanges` request exposes `ContentId` and an etag but
carries no device identifier and no local dirty-ID list
(`archive/annotation-edge4-disproven-do-not-merge:notes/2026-05-27-nickel-binary-RE-findings.md:91-103`).
So the server cannot know that some replica holds unacknowledged state.

Candidate controls, none of which are expressible in the observed protocol: per-device acknowledged
generations; a never-delete-by-omission merge mode; forcing upload before download.

[UNKNOWN] Whether Nickel merges or replaces on an authoritative response. Until hardware proves it
merges, a server-authoritative response is unsafe whenever ANY device might hold an un-uploaded
annotation — which is the normal state of a device that has been read on since its last sync.

Gating consequence: this is a second independent reason (alongside F-3b565b) that the first device
experiment must establish retention semantics before any multi-row or multi-device use.
title: Replica lost-update: a second Kobo can delete its own un-uploaded annotation
